narrative.title: Incrementing the Odometer Stored as a Chain
narrative.scenario: A legacy odometer stores its reading as a one-way chain of digits, most significant first — but incrementing must act on the least significant digit, which sits at the far end with no shortcut to it. The crew reverses the chain, runs the increment with a carry, appends a digit if the carry overflows the last node, and reverses back for display.
narrative.inputFormat: An array head of node values, each a single digit 0-9, forming a non-negative integer with no leading zeros (except the number 0 itself).
narrative.outputFormat: The digits of the number after adding 1, most significant first.
constraints: the leading digit is non-zero unless the number itself is 0

testCases.explanation: 159 + 1 = 160: the last digit rolls over and the carry dies at the tens place.
999 + 1 = 1000 — the carry survives every node, forcing a new leading digit.

hintLevels: Level 1: Addition starts at the least significant digit, which on a head-first chain is the hardest node to reach.
Level 2: Reverse once, add with a carry starting at 1, stop early the moment a carry of 0 appears, then reverse back.
Level 3: The all-nines case is the whole point of the carry loop — after the walk ends with carry 1, append a fresh node (carry becomes a single digit here since the increment adds at most 1).
